correctness.rationale: On 0<S_n<n the RU denominator is positive. If q>=t the perfect predictor treats all, so RU=0 iff the observed treat-all net benefit is the better default, exactly S_n/n>=t. If q<t it treats none, so RU=0 iff treat-none is the better default, exactly S_n/n<=t. This gives the exact sums. Matching Chernoff and Stirling bounds yield rate D(t||q), and binomial CLT arguments yield the critical and root-n limits. Exact rational reconstruction in verify.py agrees with the formulas for both branches and the equality case.
